verdicts.title: On the distribution of sensitivities of symmetric Boolean functions
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A Boolean function $f({\vec x})$ is sensitive to bit $x_i$ if there is at least one input vector $\vec x$ and one bit $x_i$ in $\vec x$, such that changing $x_i$ changes $f$. A function has sensitivity $s$ if among all input vectors, the largest number of bits to which $f$ is sensitive is $s$. We count the $n$-variable symmetric Boolean functions that have maximum sensitivity. We show that most such functions have the largest possible sensitivity, $n$. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns the distribution of sensitivity (a complexity measure) among symmetric Boolean functions, not DNF minimization or Euler characteristics of cubical complexes. It shares the 'symmetric Boolean functions' framework but says nothing about DNF-min(f) versus |χ(K_f)|.

verdicts.title: A Polynomial Time Delta-Decomposition Algorithm for Positive DNFs
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We consider the problem of decomposing a positive DNF into a conjunction of DNFs, which may share a (possibly empty) given set of variables Delta. This problem has interesting connections with traditional applications of positive DNFs, e.g., in game theory, and with the broad topic of minimization of boolean functions. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses polynomial-time Delta-decomposition of positive DNFs into conjunctions of DNFs, which shares the DNF minimization framework but does not address Euler characteristic bounds, symmetric functions, or DNF-min lower bounds via cubical topology.
